**Triage — first touch. Graded `bug`·`pm:queue`·`priority:p2`·`domain:ui`.** objectui side re-verified on `e30ed155cb71`, 03:50Z.

## What I re-verified, and what I did not

| | today |
|:--|:--|
| `FORWARD_COMPAT_FLOW_NODE_TYPES` still present | ✅ `clientValidation.ts:726`, used at `:986` |
| `sharing_rule` still opted out | ✅ `AUTHOR_SHAPE_ONLY_TYPES = new Set<string>(['sharing_rule'])` @ `:520` |
| `@objectstack/spec` resolution | ✅ still **17.2.0** in the lockfile |

⛔ **I did not re-run the `safeParse` probes.** They need an installed `@objectstack/spec`, which this checkout does not have. Those readings remain the card's, ⛔ not corroborated by me.

⭐ But the pin check matters more than a re-run would: the card measured against **17.2.0**, and the lockfile still resolves **17.2.0**. So its premises have not gone *further* stale in the four days since filing — they are as true or as false now as when written.

## ⭐ The two halves have very different costs — and the difference is a pin

- **The flow shim is unpinned.** A repo-wide grep for `FORWARD_COMPAT_FLOW_NODE_TYPES` returns exactly two files: `clientValidation.ts` and a passing mention in `ResourceEditPage.tsx:677`. **No test names it.** ⇒ if the card's "unreachable" reading holds, deletion is genuinely mechanical.
- **The `sharing_rule` opt-out is pinned, deliberately.** `clientValidation.optOuts.test.ts` guards it explicitly — `:101` names "the author-shape-only boundary (`AUTHOR_SHAPE_ONLY_TYPES`)", `:148` exercises `mode: 'edit'`, `:158` asserts `hasClientValidator('sharing_rule','create')`. ⇒ removing it is ⛔ not a one-line edit: the suite has to be rewritten on purpose, which is the right friction for switching a gate on at a security-metadata door.

⚠️ **Do not read that test's header as the boundary's definition.** It describes `sharing_rule` / `translation` / `connector` as "the three client-validation" opt-outs, while `AUTHOR_SHAPE_ONLY_TYPES` contains **one** member. Those are different mechanisms with overlapping prose. I have ⛔ not measured the other one; whoever takes this should establish which mechanism each of the three sits in before touching any of them.

## Priority

p2, driven entirely by the second half. ⚠️ Nothing is exploitable — the server still validates, so this is a **defense-in-depth** gap rather than a hole, which is why it is not p1. But the client gate is off on the exact door where, in the block's own words, *"a permissive match-all sharing condition gets written"*, and it is off for a reason that measurement says has expired. The first half alone would be p3.

## Lane

`domain:ui`: every file the fix touches is under `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/` — a published library. The contract-side repair the card was waiting on already landed **in the framework**, so ⛔ nothing here lands in `packages/types` or the spec.

⚠️ The stored-body probe against a live server that the card asks for is part of this work, ⛔ not an external dependency — so this is `pm:queue`, not blocked.
